newsitem.title: USA: U.S. help-wanted ad index rose to 88.0 in June.
newsitem.headline: U.S. help-wanted ad index rose to 88.0 in June.

text.p: The Conference Board's U.S. help-wanted advertising index rose seven points in June to 88.0 versus an 81.0 reading in May, the Conference Board said on Thursday.
The index stood at 85.0 a year ago.

"The labor market remains on a high plateau that has prevailed in the last year and a half," said Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein. "The index remains fixed in a narrow range, with the labor market expanding about as fast as it possibly can," Goldstein said.

"Given an already low 5.0 percent unemployment rate, job advertising growth remains slow, especially in the Midwest, where there is a shortage of job applicants," Goldstein said. "Today's conditions are similar to those prevailing in the late 1980s, when there were also widespread reports of jobs available and no one to fill them," he said.
Help-wanted advertising increased in six U.S. regions, with the largest gains in the Middle Atlantic (7.6 percent), East North Central (6.8 percent), and Mountain regions (3.9 percent).
Advertising declined in the West South Central (-3.3 percent), East South Central (-2.9 percent) and South Atlantic (-2.6 percent).
The Conference Board surveys help-wanted advertising volume in 51 major newspapers across the country every month.
